introduction: Eisman is most useful as a business-model and balance-sheet analyst: how does the company make money, who funds its growth, what can damage its franchise, and where does the loss ultimately land? He repeatedly turns an attractive industry story into questions about cash generation, refinancing, customer concentration and incentives.

The archive supports a more qualified assessment of him as a forecaster. There are good operating diagnoses and some clear misses, but many positions lack a price target or deadline. Interviews add expert hypotheses, not an attributable Eisman forecast every time a guest speaks. This report therefore gives you an inspectable claim ledger rather than an overall accuracy percentage.

sections.title: The strongest contribution: follow the economics
text: His AI analysis becomes valuable when it separates the vendor receiving revenue from the customer trying to earn a return. Nvidia can report excellent sales while an AI lab or leveraged data-center operator struggles to finance the next round of investment. Oracle’s cash generation versus capex is a concrete example; the same logic explains why EBITDA can hide GPU replacement costs.

sections.title: The recurring investment map
text: AI infrastructure and power supply offer visible demand; mature networks and efficient franchises offer durability; private credit and software buyouts carry less visible refinancing risk. He tests housing through affordability and incentives, banks through credit and returns on capital, and payment challengers through the difficulty of recreating a two-sided network. These are recurring analytical lenses, not a recommended model portfolio.

sections.title: Where confidence outruns evidence
text: The clearest problems arise when a plausible broad story is made to rest on an incorrect premise. Examples include subtracting a level of AI capex from GDP growth, treating political alignment as a reliable guide to a Supreme Court tariff decision, and describing a constrained supplier market as having only two competitors. A wrong supporting number does not automatically invalidate the entire investment thesis, but it weakens the reasoning used to justify it.

sections.title: His views change, and that matters
text: He explicitly revises the old rule that bank health leads the economy, shifting attention toward AI financing and private credit. The life-insurance discussion becomes less alarmed after an industry counterargument, while retaining concern about smaller or opaque structures. He also describes covering the FICO short because the balance of risk had changed. These are evidence of updating and position management; none establishes a verified realized return.

sections.title: What remains open
text: The 2027 software-refinancing thesis, the economics of sustained AI spending, and agent-driven disruption of cheap deposits or insurance distribution remain incomplete at the November 10, 2026 cutoff. Current stress, falling shares or redemption limits cannot by themselves settle the eventual default losses, investment returns or recession outcome.

sections.title: How to use this report
text: Read the framework as a checklist, then open a claim and inspect its original passage, attribution, conditions and evidence. Use the default host filter for Eisman statements and the other-speaker filter for interviews and reported views. Best and worst examples are selected for clarity and materiality, not from a tally of repeated occurrences.
bullets: A supported mechanism is not a verified profitable trade.
A dated operating forecast can be right even if the stock subsequently falls.
An unresolved causal explanation is neither disproved nor independently verified.
Publication dates, recording dates and evidence dates serve different purposes.

introduction: The strongest material takes concern operating mechanisms and funding constraints. The weakest include identifiable forecast misses and errors in the premises used to support broader views. The examples below emphasize Eisman statements; a guest being right or wrong is credited to that guest in the episode review.
This is a reasoned selection, not a performance ranking. No brokerage record, complete position sizing, tax treatment or benchmark-relative return series was supplied.

sections.title: Strong: AI demand can be real while its financing is fragile
text: His distinction between strong supplier revenue and unproven downstream returns is one of the most reusable insights in the archive. In November 2025, he identified Oracle’s need for external funding because capex exceeded operating cash flow. The filings support that funding gap. This validates the balance-sheet diagnosis, not a prediction that every AI project will fail or a particular short will profit.

sections.title: Strong: power and equipment can be the bottleneck
text: The emphasis on turbine lead times, order books and electrical infrastructure connects AI demand to tangible constraints. Equipment demand and backlog support the operating thesis. His occasional claim that only GE Vernova and Siemens supply large turbines is wrong because Mitsubishi is a major supplier; the concentrated-market thesis survives that correction.

sections.title: A clean short-horizon success: Nvidia’s next results
text: On October 31, 2025, he linked higher hyperscaler spending to very strong Nvidia results at its next release. Nvidia’s November 19 release reported $57 billion revenue, up 62% year over year. This is a relatively clear, bounded operating forecast. It should not be relabeled as a successful forecast of the share-price response.

sections.title: A bounded policy success: the September 2025 quarter-point cut
text: In the Robert Kaplan interview, Eisman explicitly agreed with a 25-basis-point September cut rather than 50. The September 17 FOMC decision matched that call. This is an attributable Eisman forecast because he affirmatively adopted it, not simply because Kaplan was his guest. It is distinct from his earlier, unsuccessful range for total cuts during 2025.

sections.title: Supported through the cutoff: no rapid easing in 2026
text: In the Ives/Verrone discussion, Eisman argued that the economy was stronger than feared and the Fed was unlikely to cut quickly. Subsequent holds and a September rate increase support that direction through the audit window. Because quickly had no precise deadline, this is a bounded assessment of the observed period, not an indefinitely valid forecast.

sections.title: Strong mechanism, unfinished outcome: software refinancing
text: He focuses on enterprise value, sponsor equity and the lender’s decision at refinancing rather than assuming that a borrower paying interest today is safe. If enterprise value has fallen, an otherwise cash-paying borrower can still need new equity or a transfer of ownership. The mechanism is sound under its conditions; the repeatedly cited 2027 realization window remains too early to grade as a completed win.

sections.title: Promising but qualified: FICO competitive erosion
text: His focus on a franchise antagonizing customers and regulators through pricing identifies a real risk. GSE acceptance and aligned loan-pricing grids establish a competitive opening for VantageScore. They do not prove that aggressive pricing alone caused the reform, that application shares equal funded-loan shares, or that every earnings and stock-price target will follow. His disclosed exit is a separate position-management event.

sections.title: Useful discipline: a cheaper payment rail still needs adoption
text: He asks why consumers and merchants would change behavior, not just whether a transfer can be made cheaply. Rewards, acceptance, convenience and the two-sided network are real analytical obstacles to disruption. The conditional adoption point is stronger than saying Visa and Mastercard are permanently immune from competition. In the crypto interview, he also usefully separates a payment network, a stablecoin and the fee token whose owners may or may not capture value.

sections.title: Clear miss: the Supreme Court tariff forecast
text: On September 5, 2025, he expected the Supreme Court to uphold the tariffs because Republican justices would defer to the president. The February 20, 2026 decision rejected IEEPA tariff authority. The political shortcut failed on the specified legal issue. His separate observation that other statutes offered tariff options was supported, so the two propositions receive different grades.

sections.title: Clear miss, with tentative wording: the 2025 easing range
text: The July 2025 discussion allowed zero, one or two Fed cuts. By year-end, the policy-rate range was 75 basis points below July, exceeding two standard quarter-point cuts. The statement was exploratory rather than a high-conviction trade recommendation, but the stated range still missed the realized outcome.

sections.title: Clear timing miss: tariffs staying on during negotiations
text: In the early Big Short team discussion, Eisman said tariffs would remain on for at least roughly a month while retaliation preceded talks. The April 9 order paused most country-specific reciprocal rates effective April 10, contradicting that timing for those rates; the 10% baseline and China escalation remained. His stronger claim that Trump was not interested in negotiating with China was also contradicted by the May agreement. These are more testable than a general warning that trade policy creates uncertainty.

sections.title: Clear policy miss: final Medicare Advantage rates
text: Eisman expected the final April 2026 announcement not to improve because of the administration’s affordability agenda. CMS instead raised the expected average payment increase from the proposed 0.09% to 2.48%. The political inference failed on the specified event. This does not itself settle insurers’ future margins, which also depend on medical costs and execution.

sections.title: Wrong investment premise: First Solar’s manufacturing credits
text: In the solar discussion, Eisman says First Solar’s subsidies will be gone by 2028. The company’s subsequent filing retains Section 45X manufacturing credits through 2032, with phase-down beginning in 2030. Different solar incentives have different deadlines. This undermines a specific bearish earnings premise; it does not independently measure the guest’s short return or prove that the stock is attractive.

sections.title: Repeated analytical error: AI capex subtraction from GDP
text: The calculation multiplies a real growth rate by a nominal GDP level and subtracts a full level of AI capex to infer almost no growth outside AI. It mixes real and nominal measures, levels and changes, and spending that may include imported or non-US inputs. Concentrated AI investment could matter greatly, but this arithmetic does not quantify its contribution. Repetition is one recurring error family, not several independent failed forecasts.

sections.title: Weak explanation: valuation cannot matter until fundamentals break
text: His reluctance to short a good company solely because it is expensive is sensible risk management. The stronger historical claim that the internet bubble first broke because of the 2001 recession is wrong: the Nasdaq peak preceded the recession. Strong businesses can produce poor returns when expectations compress, even before a reported earnings decline.

sections.title: Technical mistakes that matter to the framework
text: The reviews also correct several explanations with practical consequences: a 2:1 debt-to-equity limit supports three units of assets, not two; a 90% taxable-income REIT payout is not a requirement to distribute all cash; and a one-time capital-gains tax cannot be compared directly with an annual bond yield to declare a switch mathematically irrational. These are explanation failures, distinct from losing market calls.

The financial-literacy masterclass also omits cash from enterprise value and misstates the bridges to REIT FFO and AFFO. Its decision rules are often useful, but use the standard operating-enterprise-value and Nareit FFO definitions, plus the issuer’s own AFFO reconciliation. AFFO is not standardized.

In the Dwight Collins interview, he also claims private-equity accounting permits keeping an old mark until an exit. The inspected fund disclosure instead requires current fair-value measurement. Delayed price discovery and incentives to avoid realizing losses are different from permission to ignore fair value.

sections.title: Weak explanatory area: monetary and legal mechanics
text: The investing Q&A says ordinary deposit rates sit above fed funds and that the Federal Reserve was created by constitutional amendment. Both premises are wrong. The episode also overstates how far house prices must fall to offset a mortgage-rate increase. These errors do not erase the useful cash-flow and stock-compensation discussion, but they make independent verification essential when the analysis moves into monetary plumbing or legal authority.

sections.title: Open investment cases: Charter and Meritage
text: His February 2026 purchases have explicit mechanisms: Charter capex relief and repurchases, and Meritage valuation, buybacks and possible affordability relief. They deserve continued tracking rather than premature placement in either winner or loser lists. Charter’s later subscriber and pro forma EBITDA weakness challenges the early stabilization argument; the 2029 cash-flow and longer buyback forecasts remain open. Meritage share repurchases continue, but 2026 earnings weakened and the full-year share-count forecast is unfinished.

sections.title: An important limit on criticism
text: A vivid interview title can sound more certain than the conversation. Consumer-collapse claims, AI extinction scenarios, biotechnology outcomes and industry price targets often belong to guests. The ledger preserves those views without silently converting them into Eisman calls. Similarly, retrospective accounts of the 2008 short do not become new forecast wins in this sample.

introduction: These are recurring thesis families, with representative passages linked below. Frequency here means recurrence across the archive, not a statistical count of independent predictions. Similar claims can have different wording, timing and qualifications.

sections.title: 1. Follow the money past the exciting product
text: Demand, revenue, earnings and free cash flow are separate stages. AI equipment sales can be excellent while the buyer’s economics remain uncertain. Ask whether the company can finance the next increment of growth internally.

sections.title: 2. AI reaches far beyond technology stocks
text: Power, gas turbines, grid equipment, cooling, construction and connectivity are recurring beneficiaries. The analytical question is the bottleneck, its supply response and the length of the order book. The investment question also requires the price paid and cash conversion.

sections.title: 3. Private-credit trouble is often delayed, not absent
text: Current interest payments, a stable mark or limited redemptions do not establish whether a borrower can refinance. He repeatedly returns to software collateral values, sponsor equity, future maturities and the place where losses will be recognized. His later discussions distinguish concentrated sector stress from an inevitable systemwide crisis.

sections.title: 4. Incentives tell you where to look
text: Gross-asset fees, carried interest, affiliated transactions, aggressive pricing and underwriting incentives recur across private credit, insurance, housing and payments. Incentive conflicts provide a hypothesis to investigate. They are not by themselves proof of fraud, insolvency or a particular loss.

sections.title: 5. A durable franchise can deserve patience
text: He favors difficult-to-replicate networks and efficient business models and often holds while the operating story remains intact. High valuation alone does not usually supply his short catalyst. The tradeoff is sensitivity to overestimating durability or underestimating multiple compression.

sections.title: 6. Aggregate numbers conceal differences
text: He looks behind cap-weighted index gains, total spending, aggregate GDP and headline bank earnings. Equal-weight performance, customer income groups, business segments and credit categories can reveal divergent conditions. A market breadth gap is a useful observation, but does not itself prove the state of the whole economy.

sections.title: 7. Housing is a cash-payment and supply problem
text: Mortgage rates, home prices, income, incentives and existing-owner lock-in recur alongside land, zoning and local costs. The more useful discussions distinguish builder margins from unit sales and a weak transaction market from an inevitable collapse in all home values.

sections.title: 8. The next crisis need not repeat the last one
text: His banking background remains central, but his concern migrates toward nonbanks, AI capital commitments and insurance structures. The October 2026 abandonment of the banks-as-leading-indicator rule is an explicit framework revision. It identifies a new place to look; it does not establish where the next recession will originate.

sections.title: 9. Preserve the original thesis and watch for rationalization
text: His masterclass calls this thesis creep: the original reason for owning a stock fails, but attachment to the position produces a new excuse to hold it. The practical response is to record the thesis and the data that would disprove it. His account of holding Citi too long is an illustration of the discipline he wants, not a verified trading-performance result.

sections.title: Recurring errors deserve the same memory as recurring insights
text: The AI/GDP subtraction, overly narrow descriptions of collateral or competitors, and occasional conflation of related accounting measures recur. Do not treat confident repetition as additional evidence. Recheck the denominator, the legal rule and whether the measure is revenue, receivables, orders, backlog, income or cash.

introduction: To approximate how Eisman would approach a new situation, begin with the business and its financing, then ask what changes the story. The following is a reconstruction from the reviewed archive, not a quotation or a claim that every answer reproduces his current opinion.
A useful one-sentence version: identify a durable economic advantage, trace the cash and the incentives, locate the constraint or hidden leverage, then ask what evidence would break the thesis.

sections.title: Step 1: explain the business in plain language
text: Who pays, for what, and why cannot someone else easily take the revenue? Distinguish a proprietary product from a distribution network, a fee stream from a spread business, and a hardware sale from a customer’s recurring expense. A large total addressable market is not a valuation.
bullets: Write the customer, product, price, volume and main cost in one paragraph.
Name the switching cost, network, scale advantage or regulatory barrier.
State what would make that advantage smaller.

sections.title: Step 2: reconcile earnings with cash
text: Inspect capex, working capital, stock compensation, financing and replacement needs. EBITDA is particularly hazardous where the assets must be bought and replaced at high cost. A company showing fast revenue growth can still depend on repeated access to outside capital.
bullets: Bridge revenue to operating profit, operating cash flow and free cash flow.
Separate maintenance or replacement spending from discretionary expansion.
Include dilution and the cost of funding rather than treating financing as free.

sections.title: Step 3: find the binding constraint
text: For AI it may be power, chips, sites or funding. For housing it may be the monthly payment, land or permission to build. For a lender it may be borrower equity, collateral and refinancing access. The bottleneck often reveals which supplier has bargaining power and which customer bears the risk.
bullets: Identify the slowest input to expand.
Check who can raise prices and how quickly competitors can respond.
Use backlog and contracts carefully: an announcement, order, delivery and cash receipt differ.

sections.title: Step 4: trace the loss through the structure
text: Who owns the asset, who borrowed against it, who can demand cash, and who absorbs the first loss? A mark that has not changed is not proof of unchanged economic value. A redemption restriction does not itself prove insolvency. Look for the contractual event that forces economic losses into view, but verify the accounting separately: fair-value measurement need not wait for a sale or IPO.
bullets: Map borrower, sponsor, lender, fund, insurer and end investor.
List maturities, collateral terms, covenants and liquidity promises.
Stress both the assets and the funding rather than just reported earnings.

sections.title: Step 5: ask whose incentives distort the story
text: A manager paid on gross assets may value growth differently from an investor. A supplier can damage its franchise by extracting too much price. An affiliated transaction may need more scrutiny than an arm’s-length market price. These questions guide investigation; documentary evidence must still establish the conclusion.

sections.title: Step 6: separate the company from the stock
text: He often tolerates a high multiple while the operating story remains strong and resists shorts based on valuation alone. To use the framework rigorously, add an explicit expected-return calculation: even the right business can be a poor purchase at an extreme price. Define what price, horizon and evidence would justify holding, trimming or exiting.

sections.title: Step 7: update when the mechanism changes
text: Use new information to revise the causal map, not merely the target price. His later bank-cycle revision and moderated insurance concern illustrate that process. Guard against thesis creep: preserve the original reason for owning the stock and the facts that would invalidate it. Keep the old view and date so a revision cannot silently become a claimed original prediction.

sections.title: Worked example: an AI infrastructure company
text: An Eisman-style examination would ask whether the company owns a scarce asset or simply purchases expensive hardware; whether customer contracts are enforceable and funded; whether reported revenue arrives as cash; and whether growth requires continual debt or equity. Then compare plausible replacement costs and customer concentration with the valuation. The answer could be an attractive supplier, a fragile borrower or an excellent company priced too aggressively. The framework alone does not choose one.

sections.title: Add these checks before trusting the conclusion
text: The audit suggests several safeguards for applying the framework: verify legal assertions in the actual rule; use the correct denominator; separate real from nominal values and stocks from flows; require evidence for a causal explanation; and define a forecast deadline before grading it.
bullets: Is this Eisman assertion, a guest view, a question or a hypothetical?
What observable result would prove the claim wrong?
Does a numerical example preserve the correct units and accounting definitions?
Is the evidence contemporaneous, retrospective or still incomplete?

introduction: The recurring toolkit is primarily financial statements, industry structure and operational data. Charts provide context, but the archive does not reveal a single formal trading model or a mechanically applied technical indicator system.
The inventory below comes from transcript discussion. It does not claim that every chart shown on screen was visually inspected.

sections.title: Financial statements and company filings
text: He uses earnings releases, segment results, bank supplements and S-1 disclosures to explain a business. Relevant measures include revenue growth, margins, operating cash flow, capex, debt, customer concentration and stock compensation. Reconcile the labels: a receivable is not revenue, an order is not backlog, and adjusted earnings are not cash.

sections.title: Bank profitability and credit
text: ROE and ROTCE, price to tangible book, net interest margin, deposits, nonaccrual loans, charge-offs and reserves recur. Split investment banking and trading strength from the credit indicators that say more about borrowers. Compare valuations using consistent capital definitions and account for differences in growth and risk.

sections.title: Credit structure and funding
text: Credit spreads, maturity schedules, leverage, loan-to-value, coverage, collateral and fund redemption terms are central. For private credit, reported NAV and nonaccrual measures need context about valuations, shrinking portfolios, payment-in-kind interest and sponsor support. Distinguish liquidity, economic solvency and the timing of loss recognition.

sections.title: Valuation and expectations
text: P/E, enterprise value relative to EBITDA, free-cash-flow yield, price to sales and price to tangible book appear across sectors. The interpretation depends on capital intensity, durability and the gap between results and expectations. A valuation multiple without reinvestment requirements or a return horizon is incomplete.

sections.title: DCF as a concept, with skepticism about distant precision
text: He accepts discounting future cash flows as a valid principle, but says he dislikes building precise models decades into the future. His preferred workflow emphasizes business fundamentals and the metrics used by sector specialists. A useful adaptation is to use scenarios and sensitivity ranges rather than treat a single distant forecast as knowledge.

sections.title: Orders, backlog and industry supply
text: For power and industrial businesses, watch lead times, order intake, installed capacity, supplier concentration and backlog conversion. For AI, connect hyperscaler capex to the vendors receiving it, while checking cancellations, financing and cash collection. These indicators help distinguish near-term visibility from a permanent growth assumption.

sections.title: Market breadth and macro context
text: Cap-weighted versus equal-weight indexes, sector earnings, interest rates, Treasury yields and credit spreads help describe the market setting. They do not alone establish GDP contributions or prove why prices changed. A good dashboard presents the series and its limitations together.

sections.title: Household and housing indicators
text: Monthly mortgage payments, income, prices, builder incentives, inventories, existing-home turnover and delinquency measures recur. Separate originations from the outstanding borrower population, and payment burden from price alone. Housing-related retail and renovation activity can supply additional operational evidence.

sections.title: A compact dashboard to reproduce the method
text: For any company, use one page with business economics, cash generation, financing needs, competitive position, valuation and falsification conditions. For a sector, add supply constraints and customer health. For a forecast, record the statement date, horizon, observable test and review date before looking at the outcome.
bullets: Business: customer, product, unit revenue, contribution margin and retention.
Cash: operating cash flow, capex, working capital, stock compensation and dilution.
Funding: debt maturities, interest coverage, collateral and dependence on new capital.
Franchise: competitors, switching costs, regulation, pricing and customer incentives.
Valuation: a consistent multiple plus explicit cash-flow scenarios.
Test: the event or metric that would change the view, with a stated horizon.
